A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Statistical Early Stopping for Reasoning Models. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated examples and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of stopping rules across 12 reasoning models, mathematical and scientific benchmarks, baseline comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GPQA answerability validation, keyword-source comparisons, and stopping-horizon sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The Renewal and Maxwise algorithms, uncertainty score, keyword-selection pipeline, and matching procedure are retained. The new keyword-source experiments reuse the existing pipeline. The cold-start applicability revision concerns the reported experimental settings and does not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 expands keyword-extraction training from GSM8K alone to GPQA-only and pooled GSM8K+GPQA traces. GPQA already appeared in v1's evaluation, so this adds scientific-domain training coverage while retaining the existing evaluation domains and benchmarks.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the same prompting, Length, DEER, Entropy, linear-probe, and diagnostic PLS methods. The additional analyses introduce no new competing method; GPT-5.4 Pro serves as an answerability judge.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate a 50-item GPQA sample and its 43-item judge-filtered subset, and vary Lmax from the median to the 25th and 75th calibration-length percentiles. Appendix A.6 also narrows stated cold-start tuning from keyword/DEER/entropy signals to DEER/entropy only. This revises the reported protocol without establishing that the unchanged headline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's keyword-category and bin-size ablations, v2 tests whether scientific results survive answerability filtering, whether performance depends on keyword-extraction domain, and whether Renewal is sensitive to its correction horizon. These additions in Appendices B.1–B.2 substantially broaden the robustness questions examined.

E5.justification: The existing cross-validation and averaging practices remain unchanged. The new analyses report point estimates without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values and plotted results are retained. New results include 43/50 GPQA prompts judged unanswerable, filtered-subset performance, keyword-source FPR/power in Table 12, and Lmax sensitivity with average FPR of 1.87–2.37% and power of 61.86–64.61%. These supplement the results under altered subsets or settings rather than establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The definitions, guarantees, assumptions, and proofs in Section 2, Appendix A.4, and Appendix C are retained. Algorithm 1 and Proposition 2.1 receive equivalent notation changes. The added renewal-approximation sentence reinforces an existing caveat without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central conclusions retain the same contributions: interpretable keyword-based stopping, Renewal and Maxwise rules, conditional false-positive control, and empirical efficiency and generalization. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the filtered GPQA results as evidence against label noise being the main source of detection power, discusses domain-dependent keywords and power/FPR tradeoffs, and concludes that Lmax sensitivity is limited. Section 4 also adds discussion of downstream policies and the user-experience consequences of premature stopping.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the new answerability judge as GPT-5.4 Pro and documents reuse of the keyword-extraction pipeline. Appendix A clarifies overlapping keyword categories, explaining 104 category memberships versus 102 distinct keywords, and specifies that the Qwen3-8B abstention detector serves prompting baselines. Hardware, generation budget, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the introduction citation and bibliography entry for Suresh et al. (2025), Compute When Worth It: Risk Control for Reasoning on a Compute Budget. The remaining related-work discussion and research positioning are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative and section organization remain largely stable. Changes comprise localized appendix additions, explanatory clarifications, notation cleanup, a deployment paragraph, and updated date and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 12 and two small tables for GPQA filtering and Lmax sensitivity. Existing medical/scientific example boxes move beside their discussion in Appendix B.1, and appendix tables and figures are rearranged. Existing plotted graphics are unchanged; v1 Tables 12–15 become v2 Tables 13–16.

improvement.justification: The added analyses address previously untested sensitivity to keyword source and Lmax and partially validate the scientific benchmark's ill-posed labels. These strengthen the robustness evidence while preserving the original results. The gain is limited: GPQA validation covers only 50 LLM-judged items, and keyword-source variants sometimes exchange higher false-positive rates for higher power rather than uniformly improving performance.
